title: Elul, lived
hook: a month of preparing: a little prayer, a little honesty, a little giving
tomorrow: Yom Kippur can't fix one kind of wrong on its own. which?

segments.voice: Fifteen days of Shabbat, lived, ended on one line: keep what worked. Now the calendar turns. A new stretch begins, the Jewish year lived from the inside, starting with the month that gets you ready.

Nobody runs a race, opens a show or sits a big exam by cramming everything into the last night. You rehearse, a little, every day, until the big day finds you ready. The Hebrew month of Elul is that rehearsal: the month before Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur. So what goes in it? Three small things, it turns out: a little prayer, a little honesty, a little giving. And a story about a second try.
screen: `NOBODY CRAMS FOR OPENING NIGHT.` → `ELUL: THE REHEARSAL MONTH.` → `A SECOND TRY.`

segments.voice: Start with the story. After the golden calf, the first tablets lie broken. God tells Moses to carve two new stones like the first ones and climb the mountain again. Tradition, as Rashi tells it, says Moses went up at the start of Elul and came down on Yom Kippur with the tablets renewed. So Elul is the month of the second try, and second tries take a while. That's why Elul isn't a deadline. It's a runway. Then the three things. The High Holy Day prayer book names them in one line: teshuvah, tefillah, tzedakah. Returning, prayer, giving. Elul is where they start small. Teshuvah, a little honesty: one look at the year, one thing to set right. Tefillah, a little prayer: a few minutes a day, or one psalm. Tzedakah, a little giving: a coin, most days. Now the life part. Sometimes Elul arrives with something unfinished: a friendship that went cold, a fight at home, a promise that slipped. Elul doesn't ask you to fix it by tonight. It gives the thing a month. Something to tell a friend tonight: in the tradition, Moses carved the second set of tablets himself. Elul is the month for carving yours.
screen: `TWO NEW STONES, A SECOND CLIMB.` · `ELUL: A RUNWAY, NOT A DEADLINE.` · `TESHUVAH, TEFILLAH, TZEDAKAH.` · `SOMETHING UNFINISHED GETS A MONTH.` · then, large: `THIRTY DAYS OF GETTING READY.`

segments.voice: Make your Elul plan in three short lines: one small daily thing for prayer, one for honesty, one for giving. For each, name what will most likely get in the way, and what you'll do when it does. Then say the three lines once, out loud.
screen: `PRAYER · HONESTY · GIVING.` · `WHAT GETS IN THE WAY?` · `WHAT YOU'LL DO THEN.`

howItsDone: During Elul, Jews who keep it add a little each day: the shofar after weekday morning prayers in Ashkenazi synagogues, Psalm 27, extra giving, and taking stock of the year; Sephardi communities begin selichot prayers at the start of the month.
